1: # NL0 construction and tool template
2: 
3: Use [Audit A's shared criteria](../references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
4: as the mathematical authority. This template explains data/tool construction;
5: it is not a parallel acceptance policy. Read the [schema](../references/nl0-format.md),
6: [construction guide](../references/nl0-authoring.md), and the complete neutral
7: [submission](submission-example.md), [source application](source-application-example.md)
8: and [quantified implication](quantified-implication-example.md) examples.
9: These examples show format and derivations, not certified benchmark answers.
10: 
11: The complete [guarded-definition example](guarded-definition-example.md) shows
12: how to organize a target that includes an object's existence and a property
13: of that object. For a real a let Q(r) mean r=a. R001 first proves N001, unique
14: existence of a Q witness, without using w. D002 then defines w as that unique
15: witness with requires=[N001]. R002 takes N001 as a direct input and proves the
16: full target: unique existence and w=a. Listing D002 in the global spec does
17: not let R001 use it before its guard. Do not hide an unproved guard in a
18: restricted domain when the frozen target requires a statement on the full
19: original domain. This pattern adds no new assumption or mathematical source.
20: 
21: ## Construct one coherent candidate
22: 
23: 1. For `target` and `definitions`, extract the original H, ambient parameters
24:    and global typed definitions. Preserve the original source locations. Do
25:    not change a parameter's mathematical kind while fixing its metadata.
26: 2. For `statement_closure` and `output`, design N/R interfaces from what their
27:    consumers actually need. Put the complete formulas, quantified conditions
28:    and space identifications into the exported statement, not only its body.
29: 3. For `dependency_closure`, `argument` and `dependency_accounting`, construct
30:    each proof unit alongside its premises. List exact source inputs or display
31:    a prior local derivation for every substantive fact beyond the fixed
32:    calculations. Split when local context changes; avoid a giant S whose
33:    changing objects must later be repaired one at a time.
34: 4. For `sources` and `applicability`, inspect each selected native/primary
35:    source, preserve its complete contract and ground each instantiated premise.
36:    A signature lookup or a sentence claiming a hypothesis is true is not proof
37:    of that hypothesis. Reuse an adequate proved source rather than re-proving
38:    it; a project-specific bridge still requires its displayed derivation.
39: 5. For `object_closure` and `scope`, introduce objects and conditional premises
40:    at their actual first use. Keep witness bases and local F dependencies
41:    correct. Preserve exact coefficients and ranges when copying calculations.
42: 6. Run check_draft, correct its actual located records, inspect every own
43:    conditional packet, and report readiness below. The independent auditor
44:    applies the same criteria after definitive submission.
45: 
46: ## Canonical data shapes
47: 
48: Submit {spec,graph} using the schema, or preserve an own draft with
49: {base_candidate:N,patches:[...]}. The controller binds identity, input/pin
50: hashes, fixed language and exact native metadata; it does not rewrite proof
51: content. Use read_draft with a narrow pointer after an edit rejection.
52: Unique existing @ID/@symbol selectors work for own-stage reads/patches;
53: inserting array elements still uses numeric indices or /-. Audit evidence
54: uses standard JSON pointers instead of this selector extension.
55: 
56: For multiline changes prefer read_draft(candidate=N,pointer="/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",
57: start_line=1,end_line=20). It returns the actual numbered lines, total_lines
58: and complete text_sha256. Use an edit with exactly
59: {op:"replace_lines",path:"/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",start_line:4,end_line:5,
60: text:"replacement including its intended line endings",text_sha256:"the returned hash"}.
61: Ranges are positive and inclusive. Unselected text and line endings are
62: preserved; stale hashes are rejected. Include a line terminator when a
63: nonempty replacement precedes retained lines. Empty text deletes the range.
64: All ordinary validation and later Audit A still apply.
65: For reads only, an end beyond the string returns its remaining existing lines
66: and the actual range; the start must exist and at most 250 lines may be
67: requested. Line edits still reject any out-of-range end and never clamp it.
68: 
69: Each D has type, full definition, binders, used objects, D dependencies and
70: proved guards. Each H/E/M/N/P has full statement, definitions, binders, objects
71: and appropriate source/origin fields. Each R has direct inputs, one output,
72: definitions, rules, locals, argument and real source applications. Each S has
73: actual text, uses, earlier uses_local, objects, complete produces F statements,
74: and assumption introductions/discharges. Each source application has input,
75: at:Sddd, bindings and actual hypothesis_checks. See the linked schema/examples
76: for exact names. source_uses can serialize one already selected M/E into the
77: R.inputs, S.uses and application together; supply the actual mathematical
78: bindings and grounds yourself.
79: 
80: When a declared frozen task already supplies a complete adequate definition,
81: D.definition may be {from_task:"input ID",start_line:N,end_line:M}, just like
82: S.text. The same form is available for spec.hypotheses[i].statement when the
83: selected passage states a complete original GIVEN. Keep its origin; never
84: promote a desired conclusion or proof claim to H. An H referring to the
85: target/problem for its missing content is not standalone.
86: The controller copies those exact lines to an ordinary canonical
87: string and records their hashes; it does not select or correct the definition.
88: Still declare its objects, binders, dependencies and guards. Normalize any
89: needed notation explicitly and preserve the supplied meaning. Copying never
90: grants a property or a mathematical PASS.
91: 
92: A local declaration has symbol, type, scope, start/end, kind, declaration,
93: from_inputs, from_local and objects. from_local holds earlier F proof IDs;
94: ordinary object dependencies belong in objects. A fact proved later in this
95: same paragraph is not yet a premise for choosing its witness. State it in an
96: earlier S. In sum_{k=0}^m a(k), k is expression-bound; the free objects are a,m.
97: A k used outside the sum needs its own declaration. Statement binders are
98: recorded with that statement; a variable spanning S paragraphs uses locals.
99: Changing a ledger entry does not rename an existing formula.
100: 
101: ## Actual own-packet inspection and release
102: 
103: After structural validation call read_author_packet(candidate,inference) for
104: every R. The returned view contains the real direct input/output statements,
105: definitions, logic and own proof, plus the shared contract binding. Read the
106: output without remembering its producer body. For each factual invocation,
107: identify its actual input or previous derivation. Complete closing notes use
108: these existing evidence groups; their criterion IDs are supplied by the
109: controller from Audit A. Cite actual H/M/E/N/F/R/S or candidate locations in
110: those notes; generic assurances are insufficient.
111: 
112: record_author_checks has this exact tool form (one row per actual N/P and R):
113: 
114: ```json
115: {
116:   "candidate": 7,
117:   "readiness": "no_known_issue",
118:   "open_issues": [],
119:   "resolutions": [],
120:   "original_context_note": "Located comparison of original target/H, definitions, selected source contracts and graph closure.",
121:   "output_notes": [{"id": "P", "note": "Located check of the full output and the derivation of every clause."}],
122:   "inference_notes": [{
123:     "id": "R001",
124:     "dependency_and_local_assumption_check": "Actual factual grounds, calculation, compatible inputs and discharged assumptions, with locations.",
125:     "source_application_check": "Actual substitutions and grounds for every source premise, or why no source is used.",
126:     "declaration_check": "Actual object introductions, types, witness bases and scopes, with locations."
127:   }]
128: }
129: ```
130: 
131: These are author claims, not PASS verdicts. If an obligation is unfinished,
132: set readiness=unresolved and list an issue such as
133: {id:"I001",criterion:"dependency_closure",location:"/graph/inferences/0/argument/0/text",note:"The exact missing input/derivation."}.
134: Use not_checked for unperformed inspection; incomplete notes can be saved,
135: but cannot release the artifact. Known issues persist across candidate edits.
136: Once corrected, provide resolutions:[{id:"I001",location:"/graph/inferences/0/argument/0/text",note:"The actual correction or justified withdrawal and its grounds."}].
137: Both issue and resolution locations must exist in the current candidate.
138: The context note checks the actual definition types and their prior guards;
139: inference notes check the exact source conclusion and any needed change of
140: domain or representation, rather than listing source names alone.
141: An empty new list cannot silently erase an old issue. The program checks
142: coverage, explicit state, locations and content/authority binding; mathematical
143: soundness still needs independent Audit A.
144: 
145: An actual own-packet read remains credited after an unrelated candidate edit
146: only when its complete displayed mathematical view and acceptance authority
147: have identical canonical contents. The recorded hash covers parameters, logic, selected
148: definitions, actual direct inputs/source contracts, output and full argument.
149: Changed views require new actual reads. Current whole-candidate release notes
150: are still invalidated by every edit, and known issues still need resolutions.
151: These are same-author read receipts, never inherited mathematical verdicts.
152: 
153: Only author_release_ready allows complete-artifact submission. Otherwise
154: continue the actual local proof/source work in this same stage. At a real
155: budget limit preserve the draft as unfinished. Normal completion difficulties
156: are not a substantive mathematical-gap report. Source/graph edits invalidate
157: bound closing notes. When ready, resubmit the exact candidate. Fresh Audit A
158: receives none of these notes or historical feedback.
159: 
160: ## Library access
161: 
162: find_library_sources offers a small verified pinned metadata index, not a
163: whitelist. An exact canonical name selects that declaration; ordinary terms
164: return ranked candidates with actual matched terms. Overlap does not establish
165: applicability. probe_library resolves genuine aliases and the actual module;
166: its optional module argument is only a locator hint. Read the pinned source
167: and compare its whole native signature with its NL restatement and actual
168: application. Predicates/data definitions are not source theorems. Same-stage
169: M-label renumbering can reuse exact metadata through a disclosed mapping;
170: it does not rewrite any mathematical statement or applicability argument.
171: 
172: ## Background granularity
173: 
174: Follow Audit A's shared verified-background admission rule. Register the main
175: tools; write ordinary rigorous mathematics rather than anticipating every
176: small Lean lemma. Correct elementary compression is allowed. Audit A can
177: verify an omitted routine library fact and attach a note without an author
178: rewrite. Missing original H, source uncertainty and substantive proof gaps
179: remain blocking. These audit notes later accompany each Lean task.

1: # Audit A: per-object natural-language verification
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `nl0-audit-a-8`.
7: 
8: This section is the single authority for what an accepted NL0 must satisfy.
9: Authoring instructions explain how to meet it; the audit checks these same
10: requirements. The table IDs also name executable coverage groups. Detailed
11: definitions in self-containment, logical rules and external-theorem review are
12: annexes to these requirements, not alternative permission policies.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the original target, every original H, quantifier, domain, range, normalization, endpoint and supplied core proof route. Parameters name ambient data; they cannot hide an H or a desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | original_context_note | Give each global object one complete typed definition and each local object a legitimate scoped introduction. Prove or directly assume every construction guard before use. Defining an object grants none of its properties. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Every selected M/E has an explicit faithful full statement and verified primary/native identity, context and hypotheses. Native typeclass premises are mathematical premises too. Record inaccessible checks as UNVERIFIED; they do not support an unqualified whole-proof pass. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | H/E/M are the only proposition roots. Every N/P has one producer, every retained non-H node lies in P's AND dependency closure, and every local proof uses its actual direct inputs. Keep every original H, including an unused H, and report which are unused. An ancestor is not automatically an input. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Every input and exported N/P states all formulas, quantifiers, conditions and semantic identifications needed by its consumers. A map or identity only present in the producer's body is unavailable to another node. Original text, equation labels and external notation cannot supply content. |
21: | `object_closure` | closure | declaration_check | Reverse-check actual object occurrences against global, statement-bound or local declarations. Types, domains, witness existence, first/last use and parameter dependencies agree. A name in a ledger is not an introduction or existence proof. |
22: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Ground factual uses in direct H/E/M/N, earlier in-scope local proofs, permitted elementary reasoning, or positively checked background notes under verified-background-1. Inspect actual prose and conditions; an inventory is not its proof. |
23: | `inputs` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Direct input statements are faithfully instantiated with compatible objects and assumptions. An internal input exports exactly its stated conclusion, not its producer's unexported facts. |
24: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Establish every output clause at ordinary rigorous natural-language granularity. Check material domains, limits, regularity, uniformity, integrability, signs, constants and degeneracies. Correct routine compression needs no exhaustive elementary calculation chain. |
25: | `dependency_accounting` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Every explicit input has a real role. Record eligible omitted basic library uses as verified background notes instead of rejecting solely for missing M accounting. No unverified source, extra H, core proof or project lemma can hide in prose, definitions or typeclasses. |
26: | `output` | inference | output_notes | The proved conclusion is the exact complete exported statement under its stated hypotheses, including all consumer-needed representations and identifications. Never weaken the target or strengthen an H to close the graph. |
27: | `scope` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Introduce and discharge temporary assumptions inside arguments. Close implications, cases, negations and quantifiers correctly; no witness or local assumption escapes. Original hypotheses remain explicit H inputs. |
28: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | For every actual M/E use, give the exact substitution and a direct input or displayed earlier derivation for every premise, plus any proved bridge to the claimed conclusion. Saying that a condition holds is not grounds for it. |
29: 
30: ### Scope of the same requirements
31: 
32: Global review checks the original target/H, source authenticity and complete
33: graph: H/E/M are its roots, and each N/P has its producer in that graph.
34: Its source judgments establish identity, full-statement fidelity and source
35: conditions; they do not re-prove each consumer's application. Its structure
36: judgment checks the actual AND graph and declared producer/input boundaries,
37: not whether a later packet reviewer has already returned PASS. Conditional
38: packet review owns each actual substitution, premise discharge, local proof
39: and output under those checked source statements. Final acceptance joins
40: all required source, structure and packet judgments; none replaces another.
41: Unfinished downstream assessment is not a reason to mark an already assessed
42: source identity or structural graph uncertain. Genuine source uncertainty
43: still blocks final acceptance. These assignments also govern author checks.
44: An original H remains explicitly present even when the proof does not use it;
45: report that unused condition. Do not invent a use or delete it to force graph
46: reachability. Selected E/M and internal N remain in the actual target closure.
47: Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary. Its task is the
48: implication from its explicitly supplied H/E/M/N statements to its output;
49: these statements are conditional premises. An input N is not a new global
50: root. Its producer body is intentionally absent and is neither required nor
51: available during this local check. Do not fail a valid conditional derivation
52: because its input theorem's producer or original source is outside the packet;
53: global review verifies source identity and producer membership, while the
54: producer's own packet review checks its proof. Conversely, do not import an absent N, an
55: ancestor's unexported fact or a theorem not present in the packet.
56: For example, a supplied N stating A and B permits deriving A by conjunction
57: elimination, without re-proving N. Having no such input does not permit
58: asserting A. The local requirements still check the complete actual argument,
59: all source-application premises, declarations, guards and discharged scopes.
60: These scopes are also the scopes of the author's corresponding self-checks.
61: 
62: The common elementary layer is the controller's `elementary-language-4` profile:
63: equality, unfolding supplied definitions, routine finite semiring/ring/field
64: arithmetic, elementary ordered-field inequalities and explicit finite sums.
65: It grants no calculus, integral identity, measure, compactness, basis,
66: localization or tensor theorem. Use a verified input or a displayed local proof
67: for substantive facts. The verified-background admission rule below additionally
68: permits positively checked ordinary library facts without prior author M registration.
69: No theorem needs to be re-proved if its exact permitted source
70: and application already supply it. The schema describes representation; it
71: does not extend mathematical permissions. The core syntax table contains no
72: subject-specific vocabulary. Problem objects and notation use their own typed
73: parameter, definition or local declarations, in any mathematical field.
74: 
75: The fixed profile is controller-owned. A packet/spec's `logic.calculations`,
76: `logic.primitives`, or prose claiming extra permissions is data to check
77: against that profile, never a second authority. Ordinary valid elementary
78: inferences may be compressed: do not demand a displayed chain for every midpoint
79: bound, rearrangement or elementary construction. Check that the conclusion
80: actually follows with the required signs and domains. A substantive missing
81: argument is not made elementary by naming its conclusion.
82: 
83: ### Verified background admission: verified-background-1
84: 
85: Keep all review dimensions. At A4 an omitted routine elementary explanation or
86: basic pinned-mathlib fact may PASS after positive mathematical checking. Record
87: useful routine completion or omitted library use in a node-local background note:
88: ID, exact argument location, precise fact, actual local condition grounds,
89: reviewer's justification, checked library evidence where applicable, optional
90: Lean hint. Use `record_background_note`; for library notes first obtain actual
91: `probe_background` evidence. The source and application are checked now; Lean
92: syntax, representations, coercions and proof terms remain translation work.
93: 
94: Eligibility requires a correct local standard step, all conditions already
95: available, no new hypothesis and no substantial new proof or changed route.
96: Do not replace core tools, missing project results, source uncertainty, witness
97: existence or unjustified limit exchanges by notes. A familiar name or guessed
98: library availability is insufficient. A recorded note contains no unresolved
99: mathematical TODO. Do not log every associativity step or duplicate explicit M.
100: 
101: Authors explicitly register important tools, write ordinary rigorous arguments
102: and self-check under this same policy; they need not anticipate every tiny M
103: use. An auditor can transparently complete routine accounting without returning
104: the whole NL0 for a rewrite. The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus
105: the hash-bound audit/notes supplement. It is not an old-policy claim that every
106: dependency was explicitly registered by the author.
107: 
108: Fresh local reviewers may consult only logged read-only pinned-mathlib sources
109: in addition to their own packet and Yui rules. Preserve successful source probes
110: and actual tool readback evidence. This is
111: `fresh_packet_with_verified_background`, not old `fresh_packet_only` replay.
112: No other task, project proof, original/ancestor proof, repair history or owner
113: hint is permitted. Unverified facts remain FAIL/UNVERIFIED as appropriate.
114: Display PASS with background notes when present, retaining their count. The
115: supplement is mandatory translation input; none of its facts may become an
116: unproved Lean assumption. See [background notes](background-notes.md).
117: 
118: A calculation label alone does not establish the existence of a canonical
119: decomposition, normal form, extremizer, basis or structural identification.
120: Give the actual construction and grounds for its required properties and
121: completion, or supply a verified source with its actual application. Before
122: declaring a mathematical obstruction, check the full quantified definition
123: and the direction of the claimed bounds. One feasible value alone does not
124: establish an extremal value. A failed attempted argument is not by itself
125: evidence against the supplied proof.
126: 
127: Unfolding an explicitly supplied definition and displaying its logical
128: consequence is a local derivation; it does not need a separate source theorem
129: merely because that consequence has a familiar name. Conversely, a familiar
130: name without the required definition, premises and derivation supplies no
131: fact. Check the actual argument and identify the specific unsupported step;
132: do not replace that check with a blanket objection to a named result.
133: Distinguish a genuinely partial construction from an explicitly total
134: operation: its stated type/convention controls which existence guards are
135: needed, and totality alone grants no intended analytic property.
136: 
137: Authors construct arguments and their evidence together, then report their
138: own actual check outcomes. An explicitly unresolved or unperformed check
139: prevents release as a complete artifact. Finishing a checklist, retrieving a
140: source, passing a structural gate or asserting that conditions hold proves
141: none of the mathematical requirements. Audit A remains an independent actual
142: judgment and can find an omission the author did not recognize.
143: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
144: 
145: ## Auditor execution protocol
146: 
147: The sections below implement the shared requirements. Reviewer identity,
148: fresh packet replay, negative controls, evidence capture and verdict handling
149: are auditor/controller duties; they are not extra mathematical facts for an
150: NL0 author. Mathematical FAIL findings identify the applicable shared table
151: ID and the exact unsupported implication. If the permission boundary itself
152: is ambiguous, disclose that ambiguity rather than silently raising the bar.
153: 
154: Use [self-containment](self-containment.md) and the
155: [audit template](../templates/audit-a.md). New acceptance requires spec/graph
156: v2 and audit v3. Historical PASS records do not satisfy these requirements.
157: 
158: This audit does not use a successful project Lean build as evidence that the
159: NL proof is correct. Querying pinned mathlib for source signatures is allowed;
160: reusing the target's historical Lean proof/verdict requires explicit disclosure
161: and does not establish an independent NL audit.
162: 
163: ## A0. Freeze and disclose
164: 
165: Read the original problem and independently check `spec.json`: target,
166: quantifiers, all H roots, parameter ranges, definitions, representatives,
167: normalization, endpoint conventions, and one-target scope. No H may originate
168: from the proof writer's desired conclusion. Audit target semantics, not just
169: hash equality. Record reviewer/carrier, shared context, read artifacts, and
170: whether any reference solution was seen. Read the canonical graph, not only
171: its generated Markdown. Bind the receipt to spec/graph hashes.
172: Generate the exhaustive global index with
173: `python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py overview nl0.json --spec spec.json --out global-overview.json`.
174: It preserves every actual H (including unused or late-appended H), full global
175: statements/definitions and dependency edges with canonical pointers and hashes.
176: Read this inventory before claiming a node/condition is absent; a partial line
177: page cannot establish absence. The index supplies no verdict and does not
178: replace inspection of the relevant canonical proof and primary-source content.
179: The clean test adapter uses this same core generator, not a separate inventory
180: or mathematical standard.

1: # NL0 construction and tool template
2: 
3: Use [Audit A's shared criteria](../references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
4: as the mathematical authority. This template explains data/tool construction;
5: it is not a parallel acceptance policy. Read the [schema](../references/nl0-format.md),
6: [construction guide](../references/nl0-authoring.md), and the complete neutral
7: [submission](submission-example.md), [source application](source-application-example.md)
8: and [quantified implication](quantified-implication-example.md) examples.
9: These examples show format and derivations, not certified benchmark answers.
10: 
11: The complete [guarded-definition example](guarded-definition-example.md) shows
12: how to organize a target that includes an object's existence and a property
13: of that object. For a real a let Q(r) mean r=a. R001 first proves N001, unique
14: existence of a Q witness, without using w. D002 then defines w as that unique
15: witness with requires=[N001]. R002 takes N001 as a direct input and proves the
16: full target: unique existence and w=a. Listing D002 in the global spec does
17: not let R001 use it before its guard. Do not hide an unproved guard in a
18: restricted domain when the frozen target requires a statement on the full
19: original domain. This pattern adds no new assumption or mathematical source.
20: 
21: ## Construct one coherent candidate
22: 
23: 1. For `target` and `definitions`, extract the original H, ambient parameters
24:    and global typed definitions. Preserve the original source locations. Do
25:    not change a parameter's mathematical kind while fixing its metadata.
26: 2. For `statement_closure` and `output`, design N/R interfaces from what their
27:    consumers actually need. Put the complete formulas, quantified conditions
28:    and space identifications into the exported statement, not only its body.
29: 3. For `dependency_closure`, `argument` and `dependency_accounting`, construct
30:    each proof unit alongside its premises. List exact source inputs or display
31:    a prior local derivation for every substantive fact beyond the fixed
32:    calculations. Split when local context changes; avoid a giant S whose
33:    changing objects must later be repaired one at a time.
34: 4. For `sources` and `applicability`, inspect each selected native/primary
35:    source, preserve its complete contract and ground each instantiated premise.
36:    A signature lookup or a sentence claiming a hypothesis is true is not proof
37:    of that hypothesis. Reuse an adequate proved source rather than re-proving
38:    it; a project-specific bridge still requires its displayed derivation.
39: 5. For `object_closure` and `scope`, introduce objects and conditional premises
40:    at their actual first use. Keep witness bases and local F dependencies
41:    correct. Preserve exact coefficients and ranges when copying calculations.
42: 6. Run check_draft, correct its actual located records, inspect every own
43:    conditional packet, and report readiness below. The independent auditor
44:    applies the same criteria after definitive submission.
45: 
46: ## Canonical data shapes
47: 
48: Submit {spec,graph} using the schema, or preserve an own draft with
49: {base_candidate:N,patches:[...]}. The controller binds identity, input/pin
50: hashes, fixed language and exact native metadata; it does not rewrite proof
51: content. Use read_draft with a narrow pointer after an edit rejection.
52: Unique existing @ID/@symbol selectors work for own-stage reads/patches;
53: inserting array elements still uses numeric indices or /-. Audit evidence
54: uses standard JSON pointers instead of this selector extension.
55: 
56: For multiline changes prefer read_draft(candidate=N,pointer="/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",
57: start_line=1,end_line=20). It returns the actual numbered lines, total_lines
58: and complete text_sha256. Use an edit with exactly
59: {op:"replace_lines",path:"/graph/inferences/@R001/argument/@S001/text",start_line:4,end_line:5,
60: text:"replacement including its intended line endings",text_sha256:"the returned hash"}.
61: Ranges are positive and inclusive. Unselected text and line endings are
62: preserved; stale hashes are rejected. Include a line terminator when a
63: nonempty replacement precedes retained lines. Empty text deletes the range.
64: All ordinary validation and later Audit A still apply.
65: For reads only, an end beyond the string returns its remaining existing lines
66: and the actual range; the start must exist and at most 250 lines may be
67: requested. Line edits still reject any out-of-range end and never clamp it.
68: 
69: Each D has type, full definition, binders, used objects, D dependencies and
70: proved guards. Each H/E/M/N/P has full statement, definitions, binders, objects
71: and appropriate source/origin fields. Each R has direct inputs, one output,
72: definitions, rules, locals, argument and real source applications. Each S has
73: actual text, uses, earlier uses_local, objects, complete produces F statements,
74: and assumption introductions/discharges. Each source application has input,
75: at:Sddd, bindings and actual hypothesis_checks. See the linked schema/examples
76: for exact names. source_uses can serialize one already selected M/E into the
77: R.inputs, S.uses and application together; supply the actual mathematical
78: bindings and grounds yourself.
79: 
80: When a declared frozen task already supplies a complete adequate definition,
81: D.definition may be {from_task:"input ID",start_line:N,end_line:M}, just like
82: S.text. The same form is available for spec.hypotheses[i].statement when the
83: selected passage states a complete original GIVEN. Keep its origin; never
84: promote a desired conclusion or proof claim to H. An H referring to the
85: target/problem for its missing content is not standalone.
86: The controller copies those exact lines to an ordinary canonical
87: string and records their hashes; it does not select or correct the definition.
88: Still declare its objects, binders, dependencies and guards. Normalize any
89: needed notation explicitly and preserve the supplied meaning. Copying never
90: grants a property or a mathematical PASS.
91: 
92: A local declaration has symbol, type, scope, start/end, kind, declaration,
93: from_inputs, from_local and objects. from_local holds earlier F proof IDs;
94: ordinary object dependencies belong in objects. A fact proved later in this
95: same paragraph is not yet a premise for choosing its witness. State it in an
96: earlier S. In sum_{k=0}^m a(k), k is expression-bound; the free objects are a,m.
97: A k used outside the sum needs its own declaration. Statement binders are
98: recorded with that statement; a variable spanning S paragraphs uses locals.
99: Changing a ledger entry does not rename an existing formula.
100: 
101: ## Actual own-packet inspection and release
102: 
103: After structural validation call read_author_packet(candidate,inference) for
104: every R. The returned view contains the real direct input/output statements,
105: definitions, logic and own proof, plus the shared contract binding. Read the
106: output without remembering its producer body. For each factual invocation,
107: identify its actual input or previous derivation. Complete closing notes use

1: # NL0 and Audit A stage
2: 
3: This is stage one of Yui. It may be used independently, or its accepted artifacts may feed the translation stage. Existing production skills and historical proof verdicts are not imported by invoking Yui.
4: 
5: ## Required reading
6: 
7: Read [the data contract](nl0-format.md),
8: [self-containment requirements](self-containment.md),
9: [authoring instructions](nl0-authoring.md), and
10: [Audit A](audit-a.md) before building or accepting an NL0.
11: For conditional proofs, contradiction, cases, quantifiers, or induction also
12: read [logical packaging](logical-rules.md).
13: Read [the Lean handoff boundary](lean-handoff.md) only when preparing
14: a formalization handoff. None of these documents automatically dispatches
15: another agent or authorizes an external service.
16: 
17: ## Shared standard and execution responsibilities
18: 
19: [Audit A's shared mathematical requirements](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
20: are the single acceptance authority. Their stable IDs bind the author guide,
21: author inspection groups and mathematical audit checks. The clean author and
22: Audit A receive the same frozen section/version/hash directly. The format and
23: self-containment documents supply schemas and detailed meanings; they do not
24: expand the trusted elementary layer.
25: 
26: Author the frozen original problem using the [construction guide](nl0-authoring.md)
27: and [tool template](../templates/authoring.md). Build the actual proof,
28: declarations, source contracts and input/output interfaces together. Preserve
29: routine completion and substantive-gap handling in that guide.
30: 
31: At release, inspect the stored own packets and report actual readiness. Keep
32: known unresolved findings open until their located correction or justified
33: withdrawal. Complete notes alone do not finish authoring. An unfinished draft
34: is preserved as unfinished, without an ordinary first-acceptance audit.
35: 
36: The auditor separately performs the execution protocol in Audit A: source
37: verification, global review, fresh packet-only replay, actual judgments and
38: recorded evidence. Authors do not generate those verdicts. The NL0 author and
39: global Audit A are serial. After the global stage, independent frozen R packets
40: are reviewed with the confirmed N workers. Separate cases can run concurrently.
41: 
42: ## Execute
43: 
44: Keep `spec.json` independent of the authoring file. The canonical proof is
45: `nl0.json`; `NL0.md` and `graph.mmd` are generated views. Do not edit the views
46: as mathematical authorities.
47: 
48: ```bash
49: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py check PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json
50: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py render PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --out PATH/views
51: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py packet PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --inference R001
52: python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py audit-template PATH/nl0.json --spec PATH/spec.json --out PATH/audit-a.json

55: ```
56: 
57: Commands print JSON and return nonzero on a failed gate. `inspect-audit` may
58: successfully validate the completeness of a FAIL/UNVERIFIED record; its
59: `audit_receipt_valid` remains false and it is never an acceptance command.
60: The executable format
61: and exact meaning of the checks are documented in the data contract. Programs
62: validate explicit metadata and evidence binding; they cannot recognize every
63: undeclared theorem or prove a natural-language argument.
64: 
65: New spec/graph files use format v2 and audits use v3. Historical v1 files
66: require explicit `--legacy`; their receipts cannot establish current-standard
67: acceptance. Do not silently migrate, overwrite, or relabel old cases. The
68: archived case-2 authoring script no longer manufactures passing reviews.
69: The [format example](../../tests/fixtures/closed-addition/nl0.json) is a small schema
70: example with an unperformed audit, not a new benchmark or certification.
71: 
72: ## Verdicts and invalidation
73: 
74: - `STRUCTURE-PASSED`: schema, graph, explicit references, frozen specification,
75:   and definition prerequisites passed the mechanical checks.
76: - `AUDIT-RECEIPT-VALID`: a complete, matching audit record was checked. This is
77:   an evidence/coverage verdict, not the program proving the mathematics.
78: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED`: the named auditor actually completed Audit A for every
79:   source, definition, inference, and target obligation. Report whether the
80:   auditor shared context with the author; never relabel self-audit as an
81:   independent review or Lean verification.
82: - `DRAFT-AUDIT-CONDITIONAL`: complete review relative to explicit external
83:   statements whose primary sources remain unverified. Preserve the source
84:   warnings and follow the [conditional-source policy](conditional-sources.md).
85: - `GAP`, `SOURCE-MISMATCH`, `TARGET-MISMATCH`, `ASSUMPTION-MISMATCH`, `INVALID`,
86:   or `UNVERIFIED`: identify the exact failing obligation and affected closure.
87: 
88: Bind audit records to the canonical graph/spec hashes and evidence file hashes.
89: Changed claims, inputs, arguments, definitions, assumptions, or sources revoke
90: the affected verdicts. Version 0.3 conservatively invalidates the whole audit
91: receipt on any canonical change; fine-grained reuse is future work. Keep failed
92: reports. Never add the missing conclusion as an H, source theorem, definition
93: property, structure field, or typeclass merely to close the graph.
94: 
95: ## Deliver
96: 
97: Deliver the frozen specification, canonical graph, readable view, bipartite
98: diagram, primary-source/signature evidence, per-object Audit A, mechanical
99: results, and the first remaining gap. Describe functional smoke tests and
100: negative controls separately from mathematical review, isolation, formalization,
101: and speed experiments. Graph construction and auditing time are real costs.
102: Explicitly notify the user of every citation check deferred for inaccessible
103: primary text, including the affected E IDs, attempted retrieval routes and
104: remaining verification needs. Do not describe a partial audit as fully passed.

Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

118: /-- We say that `R` satisfies the strong rank condition if `(Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin m → R)` injective
119:     implies `n ≤ m`. -/
120: @[mk_iff]
121: class StrongRankCondition : Prop where
122:   /-- Any injective linear map from `Rⁿ` to `Rᵐ` guarantees `n ≤ m`. -/
123:   le_of_fin_injective : ∀ {n m : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] Fin m → R), Injective f → n ≤ m
124: 
125: theorem le_of_fin_injective [StrongRankCondition R] {n m : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] Fin m → R) :
126:     Injective f → n ≤ m :=
127:   StrongRankCondition.le_of_fin_injective f
128: 
129: /-- A ring satisfies the strong rank condition if and only if, for all `n : ℕ`, any linear map
130: `(Fin (n + 1) → R) →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)` is not injective. -/
131: theorem strongRankCondition_iff_succ :
132:     StrongRankCondition R ↔
133:       ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → R) →ₗ[R] Fin n → R), ¬Function.Injective f := by
134:   refine ⟨fun h n => fun f hf => ?_, fun h => ⟨@fun n m f hf => ?_⟩⟩
135:   · exact Nat.not_succ_le_self n (le_of_fin_injective R f hf)
136:   · by_contra H
137:     exact
138:       h m (f.comp (Function.ExtendByZero.linearMap R (Fin.castLE (not_le.1 H))))
139:         (hf.comp (Function.extend_injective (Fin.strictMono_castLE _).injective _))
140: 
141: /-- Any nontrivial ring satisfying Orzech property also satisfies strong rank condition. -/

spec.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
spec.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

propositions.statement: n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.

There are K-linear isomorphisms Γ:V_K→M_R⊗_R K and Δ:M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_(F_p)K. They satisfy Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c, Γ^(-1)((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗(r̄c), Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c, and Δ^(-1)([z]⊗c)=z⊗c, where r̄ denotes the image of r in K. They intertwine induced lattice operators. In particular dim_K(V_K)=n>0. Write a=ρ_K(x⊗1), d=ρ_K(y⊗1), t=ρ_K(h⊗1). On this basis aβ_0=0, aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for i≥1; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for i<λ and dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. All integers in these formulas are mapped into K. For every integer s with 0≤s≤λ, s!≠0 in K and the lattice-induced X(s),Y(s) on V_K equal (s!)^(-1)a^s and (s!)^(-1)d^s. For i,j∈I let T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost operator applied first and all scalar factors in K. Then binom(λ,j)≠0 in K and T_ij β_k=β_i when k=j and zero when k≠j. Thus T_ij are the coordinate matrix units for this K-basis.

argument.text: H001 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I consists of exactly n integers. We prove the string identities simultaneously by natural induction on t≥0. At t=0, hv=λv and xv=0 are H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v and, when t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v (with xv=0 at t=0). The relation hy=yh−2y from H002 gives h y^(t+1)v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. The relation xy=yx+h gives x y^(t+1)v=y(x y^t v)+h y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+λ−2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v, also at t=0 using xv=0. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction gives both identities for all t in their stated ranges.

produces.statement: n>0, |I|=n, and for all integers t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for all integers t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v.

argument.text: For each i∈I, repeated application of the x identity in F001 gives x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. At i=0 the product is empty and equals 1; at i≥1 its factors are positive integers, since i≤λ. Since v≠0 by H003, this shows e_i≠0 over ℂ. F001 gives h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. To prove independence, fix coefficients c and temporarily assume L2: Σ_(i∈I)c_i e_i=0. Fix j∈I and apply ∏_(k∈I,k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). Every term except j is zero; the j term is c_j [∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)]e_j. All its factors are nonzero complex numbers and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary, all coefficients vanish. Discharging L2 proves independence.

produces.statement: Every e_i, i∈I, is nonzero, h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i, and the family e:I→V is complex-linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 to the division ring ℂ, the complex vector space V, the finite index set I and the family e. F002 supplies independence, F001 gives |I|=n, and H002 gives dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n and finite dimensionality. Thus the span of e is V, so together with independence it is a basis. By F001, y^(λ+1)v has eigenvalue −λ−2 under h. Expand this vector in the basis e; comparison of each coefficient in h y^(λ+1)v=(−λ−2)y^(λ+1)v gives [λ−2i−(−λ−2)] times that coefficient zero. For i∈I this multiplier is 2(λ+1−i)≠0 in ℂ. Every coefficient is zero, hence y^(λ+1)v=0. Applying further powers of y gives all higher vanishing.

produces.statement: The family e indexed by I is a complex basis of V, y^(λ+1)v=0, and y^t v=0 for all integers t≥λ+1.

argument.text: For arbitrary i∈I divide the identities F001 by i!: x e_0=0, and for i≥1, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1). Directly y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while y e_λ=0 by F003. Also h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. These are the required integer action matrices.

produces.statement: For i∈I: x e_0=0; x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) if i≥1; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) if i<λ; y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i.

argument.text: Fix r≥0. Iterating the x matrix in F004 and dividing by r! gives X(r)e_i=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_(i−r)=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i. When r>i, iteration reaches x e_0=0 and gives zero. Similarly iteration of y gives Y(r)e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ, and gives zero past the terminating string. These binomial coefficients have nonnegative top at least r. They are integers: for every nonnegative integer a₀, the factorial expressions have boundary values binom(a₀,0)=binom(a₀,a₀)=1 and satisfy binom(a₀,s)=binom(a₀−1,s−1)+binom(a₀−1,s) for 0<s<a₀ by a common-denominator calculation. Induction on a₀, proving the assertion simultaneously for all 0≤s≤a₀, proves integrality. This establishes every divided-power formula in N001 as well as its zero cases.

argument.text: Since p is prime by H001, p≥2 and the integers not divisible by p are multiplicatively closed. Fraction addition and multiplication therefore make R a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ; in particular every integer b with p∤b is a unit, with inverse 1/b∈R. By H004 choose a simultaneous integer basis B of M and complex basis B of V. It has finitely many vectors since V has finite dimension n by H002. M010 applied to the nontrivial commutative ring ℂ supplies its strong rank condition. M003 applied to its complex basis gives that its number of vectors is dim_ℂ V=n. By N001, |I|=n; reindexing the basis by I yields the existence stated in F001.

produces.statement: There exists a family m:I→M which is a ℤ-basis of M and a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Choose m as in F001. Apply M002 with R₀=ℤ, A=M, S₀=R and the integer basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_(i∈I) of M_R. The map ι_M sends these basis vectors to m_i; a finite R-linear relation among their images is also a complex-linear relation, so all coefficients are zero. Thus ι_M is injective, identifies M_R with the R-span of the m_i inside V, and its complex span is V. For any r≥0, admissibility H004 and D005 imply X(r)M⊂M and Y(r)M⊂M; R-linearity gives preservation of M_R. In particular X(1)=x and Y(1)=y preserve M; H002 gives h=xy−yx on V, so h preserves M as well. The commutators in H002 show directly that the integer span of x,y,h is bracket-closed, since all three structure constants are integers.

produces.statement: ι_M is injective; the vectors 1⊗m_i form an R-basis of M_R of cardinality n and their images span V over ℂ. For every integer r≥0, X(r),Y(r) preserve M and M_R. Also x,y,h preserve M, and ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under brackets.

argument.text: For every integer 0≤r≤λ, apply M006 with ℓ=p and u=r. H001 supplies primality and r≤λ<p, so p∤r!. Thus r! is a unit of R. In particular λ!, j!, (λ−j)! are all units, for j∈I. Their ratio binom(λ,j)=λ!/[j!(λ−j)!] is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ−j)!/λ!. The factorials are positive and therefore nonzero as rational numbers. These statements also cover r=0.

produces.statement: For all integers 0≤r≤λ, p∤r! and r! is a unit in R. For every j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ−j)!/λ!.

argument.text: We now identify operators by their actions on the complex basis e from N001. In Y(λ)X(λ), every basis vector below e_λ is killed by X(λ); on e_λ, X(λ)e_λ=e_0 and Y(λ)e_0=e_λ. Hence Π=E_λλ. Next X(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, with coefficient binom(λ−λ+λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ. For ΠY(λ−j), an input e_k with k<j is carried below e_λ and killed by Π; if k>j the lowering string terminates and gives zero; on e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) and its image is e_λ. Therefore ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. All statements include λ=0, when every factor is the identity on the one-dimensional space.

produces.statement: For all i,j∈I, Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ and ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj.

argument.text: Combining F004, or applying it to each e_k, gives X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_ij. Invert the coefficient using F003 to get E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire statement N002.

argument.text: Use the embedding from N002 throughout to regard M_R as a submodule of V. By N001 its vectors have unique coordinates in e. Since E_ii preserves M_R by N002, the ith coordinate projection maps M_R onto J_i e_i. For any i,j∈I and c∈J_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R, giving J_j⊂J_i; the reverse inclusion follows by exchanging indices. Thus all J_i equal J. Choose the R-basis m of M_R supplied by N002. The finitely many ith coordinates of m generate J_i, since each vector of M_R is a finite R-linear combination of m, and conversely these coordinates lie in J_i by E_ii-stability. Hence J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if J were zero, every coordinate projection of M_R would vanish, so M_R would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and the nonzero basis vector e_0 in N001. Finally the maps M_R→J^I taking coordinates, and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i, are mutually inverse R-linear maps. The latter sum is in M_R since each c_i e_i is; independence in N001 gives uniqueness. This proves the direct sum decomposition without any rank assumption on a submodule of ℂ.

produces.statement: J_i=J for all i∈I; J is nonzero and finitely generated over R; M_R→J^I by e-coordinates and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i are inverse R-linear maps. In particular there is a finite nonempty family of nonzero R-generators of J.

binders.type: family in J indexed by I

argument.text: Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite nonzero R-generator family g_1,...,g_k of J from F001. The vectors 1⊗g_j span U over ℚ: tensor bilinearity rewrites q⊗Σ r_j g_j as Σ(qr_j)(1⊗g_j), for r_j∈R. M008 with F=ℚ, A=U and the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} now gives finite dimensionality of U, since this span is all of U. For injectivity of μ, write any tensor as a finite sum Σ q_l⊗c_l. Choose a common nonzero integer denominator d for the finitely many rationals q_l, writing q_l=t_l/d with integers t_l. Tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, rewrites the sum as (1/d)⊗(Σ t_l c_l). If its product in ℂ is zero, then Σ t_l c_l=0 because d≠0 in ℂ, so the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

produces.statement: U=ℚ⊗_R J is finite-dimensional, μ:U→ℂ is injective, μ(q⊗c)=qc, and its image is span_ℚ J.

argument.text: Define T=ℚ⊗_R M_R. The inclusion R⊂ℚ gives a commutative R-algebra structure on ℚ. Apply M002 to the R-basis m: the n vectors 1⊗m_i form a ℚ-basis of T. M010 applies to the nontrivial commutative ring ℚ. M003 with this basis gives dim_ℚ T=n, since |I|=n by N001.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ T=n, and the vectors 1⊗m_i indexed by I form a ℚ-basis of T.

argument.text: Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q⊗c↦q⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q⊗z the second is q⊗Σ c_i e_i=q⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ U=r_J=1.

argument.text: Choose a nonzero a∈J from F001. Then 1⊗a is nonzero in U, since μ(1⊗a)=a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent: multiplying a putative scalar relation by μ gives that scalar times a zero in ℂ. Apply M001 over ℚ to this singleton and U, whose finite dimension is one by F002 and F004. It spans U. Consequently every 1⊗g_j is q_j(1⊗a) for some rational q_j; apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. As every g_j≠0, each q_j≠0. This proves existence of the full finite rational family needed next.

produces.statement: There is a family q_1,...,q_k∈ℚ\{0} such that g_j=q_j a for every 1≤j≤k.

binders.type: family of nonzero rational numbers indexed by 1,...,k

argument.text: Choose q from F005, and fix 1≤j≤k. Write q_j=A/B with its nonzero integer numerator A and positive integer denominator B. By H001, p≥2, so p≠1. Apply M007 first to |A|≠0, then to B≠0, with ℓ=p. Choose d_N,u_N,d_D,u_D as in those applications, so |A|=p^d_N u_N, B=p^d_D u_D and neither u_N nor u_D is divisible by p. They are nonzero because A,B are. Hence q_j=p^(d_N−d_D)(sign(A)u_N/u_D). The rational sign(A)u_N/u_D and its inverse belong to R by the defining denominator condition, so this factor is a unit. This proves, for every j in the finite list, the claimed decomposition into an integral power of p and a unit of R, and therefore the existence of simultaneous finite families in F006.

produces.statement: There exist integers ν_j and units u_j∈R for 1≤j≤k such that q_j=p^(ν_j)u_j for all these j.

binders.type: family of units of R indexed by 1,...,k

argument.text: Choose ν_j,u_j from F006 and let ν be the minimum of the finite nonempty integer list ν_1,...,ν_k; choose j₀ attaining it. Such a minimum exists by repeatedly taking the smaller of two integers. Put b=p^ν a. This is nonzero, since p≠0 and a≠0. For each j, g_j=p^(ν_j−ν)u_j b lies in Rb because ν_j−ν≥0. Conversely g_(j₀)=u_(j₀)b, so b=u_(j₀)^(-1)g_(j₀) belongs to J. Thus the R-module generated by the g_j is exactly Rb, and J=Rb. Under F001, every vector of M_R is a sum Σ r_i b e_i, while any relation Σ r_i b e_i=0 has all r_i b=0 by the complex independence of e in N001, and hence all r_i=0. Thus (b e_i) is an R-basis. The same spanning and independence argument works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001, F002 and F004 this proves N003.

argument.text: By H001, an integer maps to zero in K exactly when divisible by p. Thus for a/b∈R the denominator has nonzero image in K, and φ(a/b)=(a·1_K)(b·1_K)^(-1) is defined. Equality of fractions follows by cross multiplication, so the formula is well-defined and preserves addition, multiplication and 1. The same formula in F_p gives ψ:R→F_p. It is onto, since every integer residue occurs, and its kernel is pR: ψ(a/b)=0 is equivalent to p∣a, hence a/b=p((a/p)/b). Conversely multiples of p have zero image. The induced map R/pR→F_p is therefore a bijective ring map. Both constructions agree with the usual inclusion F_p→K. Every unit of R has nonzero image in K, since its image has a multiplicative inverse. In particular N002 shows that r! for 0≤r≤λ and binom(λ,j), j∈I, have nonzero images in K.

produces.statement: φ:R→K and ψ:R→F_p are unital ring maps extending the integer maps, ψ is surjective with kernel pR, R/pR≅F_p, and for 0≤r≤λ and j∈I the elements r! and binom(λ,j) have nonzero images in K.

argument.text: Define Γ and Γ' by Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c and Γ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗φ(r)c. The defining ℤ-balancing relations in R⊗_ℤ M and in M⊗_ℤ K, and the R-balancing relation in M_R⊗_R K, show that these formulas extend to K-linear maps. They are inverse: Γ'Γ(m⊗c)=m⊗c, and ΓΓ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗φ(r)c=(r⊗m)⊗c. These tensors generate, so the composites are identities. Next define Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c and Δ'([z]⊗c)=z⊗c. Because p acts as zero on K, changing the lift z by pz' changes the second formula by pz'⊗c=z'⊗pc=0. Using F001, scalar balancing in F_p=R/pR gives the remaining balancing condition; thus both maps are well-defined and K-linear. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. This proves the two scalar-extension isomorphisms with exactly the formulas in N004. An operator preserving M extends on all these tensors by applying it to the lattice factor; the displayed formulas commute with that operation. For Δ this also holds for any R-linear operator of M_R, since it preserves pM_R.

produces.statement: Γ and Δ are K-linear isomorphisms with Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c, Γ^(-1)((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗φ(r)c, Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c, and Δ^(-1)([z]⊗c)=z⊗c. They commute with the induced lattice operators (and Δ with all R-linear endomorphisms of M_R).

argument.text: Choose b≠0 with J=Rb from N003. That input proves that (b e_i)_(i∈I), regarded in M_R via the injective map ι_M of N002, is an R-basis. Apply M002 with R₀=R, S₀=K and this basis, using φ from F001. It yields the K-basis (1⊗b e_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The tensor flip z⊗c↦c⊗z is K-linear, well-defined by balancing, and inverse to the reverse flip. Therefore (b e_i⊗1) is a basis of M_R⊗_R K. Transporting it by Γ^(-1) gives the K-basis β_i defined above: inverse linear maps carry spanning families to spanning families and relations to the same relations. Apply M010 to the nontrivial commutative field K, then M003 to β to obtain dim_K V_K=|I|=n>0 using N001.

produces.statement: b∈J, b≠0, J=Rb, and β_i=Γ^(-1)((b e_i)⊗1), i∈I, is a K-basis of V_K; dim_K V_K=n>0.

argument.text: Put a=ρ_K(x⊗1), d=ρ_K(y⊗1), t=ρ_K(h⊗1). By N001, complex linearity gives x(b e_i)=b x e_i, y(b e_i)=b y e_i, and h(b e_i)=b h e_i. N002 guarantees all these lattice operations are defined, and F002 transports their tensors. Thus aβ_0=0; aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for i≥1; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for i<λ, dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The coefficients are the images of the same integers in K. The identical reasoning using N001 for X(r),Y(r) gives their integral divided-power matrices on this basis for all r≥0, including the stated zero cases. Likewise each E_ij preserves M_R by N002 and acts there by E_ij(b e_k)=δ_jk b e_i, so its scalar extension, transported by Γ^(-1), is the coordinate matrix unit of β.

produces.statement: On the K-basis β, aβ_0=0; aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ; dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i for i∈I. The induced X(r),Y(r) have the divided-power matrices X(r)β_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)β_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise, and Y(r)β_i=binom(i+r,r)β_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. The scalar-extended E_ij, transported to V_K, send β_k to δ_jk β_i.

argument.text: Fix 0≤r≤λ. As operators on M, the characteristic-zero definitions give r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r; N002 gives their preservation of M. Tensoring these equalities gives the same equalities of induced operators on V_K. By F001, r!≠0 in K, so the induced divided powers equal (r!)^(-1)a^r and (r!)^(-1)d^r. The equality E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)Y(λ)X(λ)Y(λ−j) in N002 is an equality of R-linear operators on M_R. Extending scalars and transporting by Γ^(-1) preserves sums and compositions: this follows directly by evaluating on each pure tensor z⊗c. Substitute the divided-power equalities, whose indices λ−i, λ, λ−j all lie between 0 and λ. The result is T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost factor applied first. Every scalar inverse exists by F001. F004 gives T_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i. Along with F001–F004 this proves every assertion of N004, including the two natural tensor identifications and positive dimension.

argument.text: N002 proves x,y,h preserve M and their integer span is a Lie algebra, which supplies the construction guard for ρ_K. Choose β from N004; set a,d,T as declared. N004 states that every scalar inverse in the polynomial T exists and T_ijβ_k=δ_jkβ_i. Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1). Thus a and d preserve W. Repeated composition shows by finite induction that every nonnegative power of either preserves W; the identity also preserves W. Composing these powers and multiplying by K-scalars preserves W by the subspace axioms. Every polynomial T_ij in N004 therefore preserves W.

produces.statement: For all i,j∈I, T_ij preserves W, and T_ijβ_k=δ_jkβ_i for k∈I.

argument.text: First temporarily assume L3: W={0}. Then the disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately; discharge L3, giving F002. For the other branch temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. By this inequality and the subspace zero axiom, some nonzero vector lies in W. Expanding it in the basis β gives coefficients in K. original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

original_context.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

argument.text: H001 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I consists of exactly n integers. We prove the string identities simultaneously by natural induction on t≥0. At t=0, hv=λv and xv=0 are H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v and, when t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v (with xv=0 at t=0). The relation hy=yh−2y from H002 gives h y^(t+1)v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. The relation xy=yx+h gives x y^(t+1)v=y(x y^t v)+h y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+λ−2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v, also at t=0 using xv=0. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction gives both identities for all t in their stated ranges.

argument.text: For each i∈I, repeated application of the x identity in F001 gives x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. At i=0 the product is empty and equals 1; at i≥1 its factors are positive integers, since i≤λ. Since v≠0 by H003, this shows e_i≠0 over ℂ. F001 gives h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. To prove independence, fix coefficients c and temporarily assume L2: Σ_(i∈I)c_i e_i=0. Fix j∈I and apply ∏_(k∈I,k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). Every term except j is zero; the j term is c_j [∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)]e_j. All its factors are nonzero complex numbers and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary, all coefficients vanish. Discharging L2 proves independence.

produces.statement: Every e_i′, i′∈I, is nonzero, h e_i′=(λ−2i′)e_i′, and the family e:I→V is complex-linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 to the division ring ℂ, the complex vector space V, the finite index set I and the family e. F002 supplies independence, F001 gives |I|=n, and H002 gives dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n and finite dimensionality. Thus the span of e is V, so together with independence it is a basis. By F001, y^(λ+1)v has eigenvalue −λ−2 under h. Expand this vector in the basis e; comparison of each coefficient in h y^(λ+1)v=(−λ−2)y^(λ+1)v gives [λ−2i−(−λ−2)] times that coefficient zero. For i∈I this multiplier is 2(λ+1−i)≠0 in ℂ. Every coefficient is zero, hence y^(λ+1)v=0. Applying further powers of y gives all higher vanishing.

produces.statement: The family e indexed by I is a complex basis of V, y^(λ+1)v=0, and y^t′ v=0 for all integers t′≥λ+1.

argument.text: For arbitrary i∈I divide the identities F001 by i!: x e_0=0, and for i≥1, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1). Directly y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while y e_λ=0 by F003. Also h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. These are the required integer action matrices.

Fix r≥0. Iterating the x matrix in F004 and dividing by r! gives X(r)e_i=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_(i−r)=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i. When r>i, iteration reaches x e_0=0 and gives zero. Similarly iteration of y gives Y(r)e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ, and gives zero past the terminating string. These binomial coefficients have nonnegative top at least r. They are integers: for every nonnegative integer a₀, the factorial expressions have boundary values binom(a₀,0)=binom(a₀,a₀)=1 and satisfy binom(a₀,s)=binom(a₀−1,s−1)+binom(a₀−1,s) for 0<s<a₀ by a common-denominator calculation. Induction on a₀, proving the assertion simultaneously for all 0≤s≤a₀, proves integrality. This establishes every divided-power formula in the exported conclusion as well as its zero cases.

argument.text: We now identify operators by their actions on the complex basis e from N001. In Y(λ)X(λ), every basis vector below e_λ is killed by X(λ); on e_λ, X(λ)e_λ=e_0 and Y(λ)e_0=e_λ. Hence Π=E_λλ. Next X(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, with coefficient binom(λ−λ+λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ. For ΠY(λ−j), an input e_k with k<j is carried below e_λ and killed by Π; if k>j the lowering string terminates and gives zero; on e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) and its image is e_λ. Therefore ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. All statements include λ=0, when every factor is the identity on the one-dimensional space.

Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire statement the exported conclusion.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.

argument.text: Use the embedding from N002 throughout to regard M_R as a submodule of V. By N001 its vectors have unique coordinates in e. Since E_ii preserves M_R by N002, the ith coordinate projection maps M_R onto J_i e_i. For any i,j∈I and c∈J_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i∈M_R, giving J_j⊂J_i; the reverse inclusion follows by exchanging indices. Thus all J_i equal J. Choose the R-basis m of M_R supplied by N002. The finitely many ith coordinates of m generate J_i, since each vector of M_R is a finite R-linear combination of m, and conversely these coordinates lie in J_i by E_ii-stability. Hence J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: if J were zero, every coordinate projection of M_R would vanish, so M_R would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and the nonzero basis vector e_0 in N001. Finally the maps M_R→J^I taking coordinates, and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i, are mutually inverse R-linear maps. The latter sum is in M_R since each c_i e_i is; independence in N001 gives uniqueness. This proves the direct sum decomposition without any rank assumption on a submodule of ℂ.

argument.text: Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite nonzero R-generator family g_1,...,g_k of J from F001. The vectors 1⊗g_j span U over ℚ: tensor bilinearity rewrites q⊗Σ r_j g_j as Σ(qr_j)(1⊗g_j), for r_j∈R. M008 with F=ℚ, A=U and the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} now gives finite dimensionality of U, since this span is all of U. For injectivity of μ, write any tensor as a finite sum Σ q_l⊗c_l. Choose a common nonzero integer denominator d for the finitely many rationals q_l, writing q_l=t_l/d with integers t_l. Tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, rewrites the sum as (1/d)⊗(Σ t_l c_l). If its product in ℂ is zero, then Σ t_l c_l=0 because d≠0 in ℂ, so the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

argument.text: Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q⊗c↦q⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q⊗z the second is q⊗Σ c_i e_i=q⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ U=r_J=1.

argument.text: Choose a nonzero a∈J from F001. Then 1⊗a is nonzero in U, since μ(1⊗a)=a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent: multiplying a putative scalar relation by μ gives that scalar times a zero in ℂ. Apply M001 over ℚ to this singleton and U, whose finite dimension is one by F002 and F004. It spans U. Consequently every 1⊗g_j is q_j(1⊗a) for some rational q_j; apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. As every g_j≠0, each q_j≠0. This proves existence of the full finite rational family needed next.

argument.text: Choose q from F005, and fix 1≤j≤k. Write q_j=A/B with its nonzero integer numerator A and positive integer denominator B. By H001, p≥2, so p≠1. Apply M007 first to |A|≠0, then to B≠0, with ℓ=p. Choose d_N,u_N,d_D,u_D as in those applications, so |A|=p^d_N u_N, B=p^d_D u_D and neither u_N nor u_D is divisible by p. They are nonzero because A,B are. Hence q_j=p^(d_N−d_D)(sign(A)u_N/u_D). The rational sign(A)u_N/u_D and its inverse belong to R by the defining denominator condition, so this factor is a unit. This proves, for every j in the finite list, the claimed decomposition into an integral power of p and a unit of R, and therefore the existence of simultaneous finite families in F006.
